front: When is fetal echocardiography optimally performed?
back: At 18–20 weeks' gestation. This balances fetal size (large enough to image), amniotic fluid, and rib ossification.

front: When is fetal cardiac embryologic development complete?
back: By approximately 8 weeks' gestation. All chambers and outflow tracts are formed.

front: List four indications for fetal echocardiography.
back: 1) Prior child with CHD or maternal CHD. 2) Suspected fetal arrhythmia or hydrops. 3) Suspected cardiac defect on OB screening ultrasound. 4) Maternal diabetes or teratogen exposure (lithium — Ebstein's; retinoic acid).

front: Which cardiac lesion is classically hard to detect on fetal echo, and why?
back: Coarctation of the aorta — the large fetal ductus arteriosus supplies flow to the descending aorta and masks the coarctation until postnatal ductal closure.

front: Which types of ASD are difficult to detect on fetal echo?
back: Secundum ASD — the normal fetal patent foramen ovale (right-to-left shunt) can mimic and mask a true secundum ASD until postnatal life.

front: Which cardiac abnormality is classically caused by maternal lithium exposure?
back: Ebstein's anomaly of the tricuspid valve.

front: Which cardiac lesion is associated with maternal diabetes?
back: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy of the newborn (transient, resolves in the first months of life). Also increased risk of transposition, VSD, and truncus arteriosus.
